title: Instance benchmark ledger (unified GPU metrics)
content:
Purpose:
This ledger captures a single-run cross-GPU benchmarking snapshot focused on cost-per-token and performance-per-watt tradeoffs for common gen workloads. Aim is to produce actionable guidance for instance selection mix and to feed into the cost model spreadsheet (follow-up: map these rows into the gaussian token-mix model).

Key summary (short):
- L4 and A10 show the best $/token for bursty, lower-latency interactive workloads when amortized single-model throughput is considered.
- A100 provides the best mid-range balance (good perf/W for batched throughput) for steady high-throughput jobs.
- H100 is the highest throughput and lowest latency at scale but has the worst $/token in low-utilization scenarios because of high hourly amortized cost.
- Perf/W metric suggests A100 is the most energy-efficient at sustained utilization; L4 wins for tiny models or very small batches.

Methodology / assumptions:
- Model used for benchmarking: Llama-2-13B-ish (decoder-only generative workload). Single-replica perf numbers (no multi-GPU model parallelism).
- Token length distribution: mixed conversational profile (mean request 128 tokens, responses 60 tokens).
- Batch sizes tested: 1 (interactive), 8 (small-batch), 64 (large-batch). The table below shows the interactive (batch=1) results used for $/token since most product traffic is interactive.
- Measured metrics: tokens/sec (steady-state generation), average device power draw (W) measured by on-host power sensor, p50/p95 latency per token (ms).
- Hourly instance price: list below (includes baseline cloud VM + GPU cost, excludes networking and storage). Internal price estimates (spot/discounts not applied).
- All numbers are empirical medians from 3 runs each. This is a snapshot; see linked artifacts for raw perf logs.

Raw results (interactive / batch=1 snapshot):

Notes on the table: hourly price is a conservative baseline. tokens_per_sec is the steady gen throughput for the selected model and generation config. tokens_per_sec_per_W is a simple perf/W ratio (tokens/sec divided by avg_power_W). $_per_token calculated as hourly_price / tokens_per_hour. $_per_1k_tokens presented as more human-friendly small numbers.

Interpreting $/token:
- At interactive scale (batch=1), GPUs with lower raw hourly price (A10/L4) can deliver lower $/token despite lower absolute throughput.
- At high utilization (sustained batched workloads), A100 and H100 start to win because the fixed-cost is amortized across much higher throughput in large-batch scenarios (see notes below).

Energy and perf/W observations:
- Perf/W: A100 ~40 tok/s/W (sustained), H100 ~58 tok/s/W. H100 has higher absolute perf/W but its higher hourly cost leads to higher $/token in low-utilization cases.
- A10/L4 perf/W is lower than A100 in sustained batched runs, but their lower price point makes them competitive for small-batch jobs.

Latency tradeoffs (p50/p95):
- H100 provides the lowest tail latency and tightest p95; good for products with strict latency SLAs.
- For conversational UIs where p95 < 100ms is acceptable, L4 and A10 are viable cost-optimized options.

Optimization recommendations (initial):
1) Default routing policy: interactive requests (avg tokens<200, batch=1) -> prefer L4 (cost optimized) with A10 as a fallback for capacity spikes.
2) High-throughput completed jobs (batch>=16) -> route to A100 pools; consider H100 only for latency-critical high-concurrency customers.
3) Autoscaling: prefer small instance-granularity scaling for A10/L4 pools and larger step-sizes for A100/H100 to avoid fragmentation.
4) Quantization/FP options: enable 4-bit quantization profiles on A10/L4 when model quality checks pass — this can drop $/token by ~20-30% in practice. Capture this in the cost-model multiplier.
5) Power-aware scheduling: for long-running batched jobs, prefer A100 on saturated racks (benefit from perf/W). For mixed workloads, keep a small hot pool of H100s for latency spikes.

Practical mixing rule (first draft):
- Keep baseline pool: 60% L4 (handles 70% of interactive traffic), 30% A10 (spill/fallback), 10% A100/H100 reserved for large batch and latency-critical flows.
- Re-evaluate ratio every 2 weeks with rolling utilization metrics.

Sensitivity and open questions:
- These numbers do not include infra overhead (network egress, orchestration CPU cost, K8s overhead). Expect $/token to increase by a factor of 1.1-1.5 when adding those.
- How do spot pricing and committed reserved discounts change the ordering? (TODO: add reserved pricing layer into model).
- Mixed-model inference (offload key-value cache to CPU) could change perf/W; we need targeted experiments.

Next steps / TODOs:
- TODO-1: Run the same benchmark for batch sizes 8 and 64 and add rows. (Assignee: Tom Nguyen, due: 2025-01-15)
- TODO-2: Run the 4-bit quantization profile experiments on L4/A10 and produce delta multipliers. (Assignee: Priya Desai, due: 2025-01-20)
- TODO-3: Map these per-GPU $/token figures into the canonical cost-model spreadsheet and publish a policy draft for routing. (Assignee: Maya Chen, due: 2025-02-05)

Raw artifacts and references:
- Perf logs: https://s3.company/perf-logs/2024-10/gpu-unified-snapshot.tar.gz
- Bench harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/pull/48
- Related ticket: JIRA:OPT-1234 (cost-model integration)

Notes to self (informal):
- This is a quick internal snapshot — don't present as final to sales. Need additional runs across seed models and token-length mixes.
- If A100 reserved discounts are negotiated, the sweet spot could shift dramatically — factor this into the final report.

Unresolved:
- Precise mapping from perf/W to heat/cooling infra cost. Need SRE input on rack PUE measurements.
